question.leadin: This king first swore allegiance to Edward Longshanks of England in 1296.
question.text: Name this king who eventually won his country's independence from England in 1327.
question.clue: This ruler was excommunicated after killing John Comyn in a church, but he solidified his power by marrying his son David II to Joan and ensuring a 5-year truce in the Treaty of Northampton.

swap.leadin: This poet's rivalry with John Keats was so intense that he used the poem Don Juan [don JOO-an] to mock him after death, claiming that Keats had died from reading a bad review of his work instead of from tuberculosis.
swap.text: Name this English Romantic poet. Keats was convinced that this nobleman had bought good reviews for works like Childe Harold's Pilgrimage.
swap.answerHtml: Lord Byron (accept George Gordon, Lord Byron; accept George Gordon Noel Byron, sixth Baron Byron)
swap.clue: This commander who, in April 1824, died of a fever in Missolonghi before he could execute an attack on Lepanto.

question.text: This English privateer dubbed his victory at Cadiz "singeing the King of Spain's beard." This captain of the Golden Hind completed the second circumnavigation of the Earth.
question.clue: The mojito was invented during this man's victory at Cartagena de Indias, which happened before he evacuated the original Roanoke colony.

swap.leadin: In addition to being a British Prime Minister, this man also wrote novels.
swap.text: This man rose to power when his party was divided over the decision to repeal the Corn Laws, and was the only British Prime Minister of Jewish birth.
swap.clue: While not in politics, this man authored the novel Sybil, or the Two Nations.

question.leadin: Answer these questions regarding the Norman conquest of England.
question.text: The conquest was led by this Duke of Normandy who defeated Harold Godwinson in 1066.
question.answerHtml: William the Conqueror [prompt on “William”; accept William Ior William the Bastard]
question.clue: This man received a blessing from Pope Alexander II to perform his most famous action, which he claimed was sanctioned by Edward the Confessor.

swap.text: The Jacobites became active after this event, in which James II was overthrown due to his Catholic sympathies. The English Bill of Rights was adopted in the wake of this event.
swap.clue: Irish resistance to this event ended at the Battle of the Boyne.

question.text: This woman brought down James Callaghan's government in 1979 with a vote of no confidence. She led Britain for the next eleven years as its first female prime minister.
question.clue: This politician authored a "Conservative Manifesto" and is the namesake of an ideology often paired with Reaganomics.

swap.text: After the 2017 snap British election, Theresa May was forced to form a coalition with the Democratic Unionist Party, which only holds seats in this constituent country of the UK with capital at Belfast.
swap.answerHtml: Northern Ireland [do not accept or prompt “Ireland” or “Republic of Ireland”]
swap.clue: The "blanket" and "dirty" protests at this region's Maze Prison culminated in a hunger strike led by Bobby Sands.

question.leadin: Identify these British prime ministers from the age of Victoria.
question.text: This man served as prime minister four times between 1868 and 1894. Noted for his support of Irish Home Rule, this member of the Liberal Party was a rival of Benjamin Disrael.
question.clue: This politician verbally attacked a rival for doing nothing against the "Bulgarian Horrors" during his Midlothian Campaign.

swap.leadin: This man gained power after leading a coup against Roger Mortimer, whom he killed at Nottingham Castle with the help of the Earl of Salisbury.
swap.text: Name this king, who ruled during England's victories at Crecy and Neville's Cross as well as the opening of the Good Parliament.
swap.clue: Under this king, the Statute of Laborers was introduced as an attempt to keep wages low despite major population loss caused by the Black Death.

question.text: Mick McGahey called Reid "broken" due to Reid's opposition to one of these events in 1984. Reid favoured holding a national ballot one of these events which included the Battle of Orgreave which was led by Arthur Scargill.
question.answerHtml: coal miners’ strike [prompt strike by asking “in what industry?”]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Britain's involvement in World War II.
swap.text: This is the name of the plan the Nazi government had developed for invading England.
swap.clue: This was the codename for the Nazi invasion of the British isles. Due to British air superiority after losing the 1940 Battle of Britain, the Germans never followed through on the plan.

question.leadin: You are a wealthy member of the European bourgeoisie in 19th century Europe. Answer some questions about expanding and profiting off of land ownership.
question.text: You can grab some land in the Scottish Highlands through this process of appropriation of common land. After a General Act regarding this process, commissioners could approve areas for it without consulting parliament.
question.clue: The terms "Levellers" and "Diggers" originally referred to people who took action against this practice.

swap.leadin: Traditions including the "wooden horse", which entailed tying a criminal to a wooden frame and parading around the village, inspired these events.
swap.text: Name these 1839-1843 riots during which farmers dressed up as its namesake women and destroyed toll-gates to protest unfair taxation.
swap.clue: Thomas Bullin's tax raises along roads in Wales led to these riots in which poor Welsh men cross-dressed and destroyed toll-gates.

question.leadin: Answer some questions on the economic history of the counties of Kent, Sussex, and Dorset.
question.text: The Mermaid and Olde Bell inns in this town were connected by a secret passage and used by the Hawkhurst Gang. This town replaced New Romney as one of the Cinque Ports after the River Rother changed course.

swap.leadin: Name the following naval battles of World War I.
swap.text: This battle between battlecruiser squadrons off the coast of England almost resulted in a crushing British victory until a misinterpreted signal caused the ships to break off pursuit.
swap.clue: This 1915 North Sea battle saw the British sink the German cruiser Blucher. Its namesake location was previously the site of a 1904 incident when Russian ships mistook British trawlers for the Japanese Navy, resulting in three deaths and a serious diplomatic incident.

question.leadin: James Allen's extension of this policy to Waikato-Maniapoto outraged locals who accused the government of illegally using census data.
question.text: Name this policy that local men circumvented with the help of Princess Te Puea ("teh PWAY-uh"). In Canada, this policy was opposed by Henri ("awn-REE") Bourassa during a namesake "crisis" in 1917.
question.answerHtml: conscription into the British military [accept British World War I draft; accept Conscription Crisis of 1917]

swap.text: The lack of approval from the Australian government meant that Parliament could not force secession because of this 1931 act. This act granted legislative equality to British dominions, effectively forming the Commonwealth.

question.leadin: The slang and code of miners of this ethnicity in towns like Real del Monte is thought to be a major influence on albur, a form of Mexican wordplay featuring double entendres.
question.text: Name this ethnicity of the miners who founded Mexico's oldest football club in Pachuca. Emigrants of this ethnicity were often nicknamed "cousin Jacks" when working in areas like South Australia's Copper Coast and Michigan's Upper Peninsula.

swap.leadin: In discussing her love for her subjects, the speaker of this speech claimed "There is no jewel, be it of never so rich a price, which I set before this jewel."
swap.text: Name this 1601 speech which promised reform in response to parliamentary opposition to royal monopolies.
